suggestions.title: Weigh in tomorrow morning — nine days carried, and the fat-or-water verdict dies Tuesday

rationale.science: A morning weight — after the bathroom, before food — is comparable day to day because normal water swings run a pound or two on their own (sodium, carbs and creatine move scale weight, not fat; DASH-Sodium/Juraschek 2020 family). That consistency is what lets a single read re-anchor a damped trend.
rationale.data: Last read 8/21 at 162.4. The trend has been carried at 162.9 for nine days, and your app's own gap row prices your rate anywhere from standing still to about 0.75 lb/wk of loss — a range that includes zero.
rationale.relationship: One read collapses that range back to a number, grades the fat-or-water verdict before it files unanswered on Tuesday, and — with a meal log beside it — hands the maintenance fit its first matched day in ten. No other single entry does that much.

suggestions.predict: Mid-162s: the drop was fat, and low-162s comes into play. Low 163s: the water giveback ran bigger than the tape caught — still on script. Above 163.5: I over-read it and will say so. No read by Tuesday: the verdict files void — unanswered, not wrong.

suggestions.title: Put the week on paper — sessions if any happened, or one line: 'rest week'

rationale.science: Layoffs up to about two weeks cost a trained lifter essentially nothing, and what is lost returns quickly (Bosquet 2013; Ogasawara 2013). Your cheap window runs to about Friday.
rationale.data: Last session 8/21 — day nine with nothing on the sheet, and four fresh baselines plus the hip-thrust target still waiting for their first occasion.
rationale.relationship: One line turns an unreadable hole into a planned deload and sets the comeback session up to grade as baselines, not declines — openers at 1–2 reps in reserve, the rule that released the last two holds.

suggestions.predict: With the line written, the comeback session reads clean against fresh baselines. Still blank by Friday: the free window closes and the next brief becomes a comeback plan.

suggestions.title: Restart the food log today — forward only, don't reconstruct the nine blank days

rationale.science: Self-monitoring is the strongest single predictor of results on a cut — when a rate stalls, adherence explains it far more often than metabolism (Alhassan 2008). Meals reconstructed from a week-old memory are guesswork, and bad entries are worse than blanks.
rationale.data: Last meal on paper is 8/20 — 2,700 kcal, 180 g protein. The 8/21–8/22 back-fill window expired today with both days still blank, and the app's maintenance estimate has already slid on the empty stretch.
rationale.relationship: The maintenance math runs on matched days — a meal log and a weigh-in together. Every clean day from today forward rebuilds it; the old blanks can stay blank.

suggestions.predict: Two or three matched days and the maintenance estimate stops sliding and re-prices on real food. Still dark: it keeps drifting, and I keep reading every move in it as an artifact of the empty window, not news about your body.
